text:
marie: heads-up — seeing intermittent IOPS spikes on eu-west2 GPU pool. nvme device /dev/nvme3 is getting read errors and our scrubber is marking small ranges as badblocks, which then triggers eviction on a handful of pods. GPU attaches started failing around 09:04 UTC.

vikram: ack. do we have a pattern? same host group / kernel version?

marie: looks concentrated to gnode* in eu-west2-b. same kernel (5.15.0-88). errors started after last night's storage-agent deploy. not sure if scrubber threshold got more aggressive.

carla: can you paste the dmesg and scrub logs?

marie: sure — snippet below: 

```
May 14 09:02:17 gnode-45 kernel: nvme nvme3: I/O error, read qid 0
May 14 09:02:18 gnode-45 storage-scrubber[1423]: flagged 16 blocks bad (/dev/nvme3p1) bloom_ok=false
May 14 09:02:19 gnode-45 kubelet: Pod gpu-job-211 failed attach: local-disk error: device busy
May 14 09:02:22 gnode-47 kernel: nvme nvme3: retrying R/NM for read
```

marie: scrubber logs show bloom-check failures — small ranges (4-64KB) repeatedly. but SMART shows no media reallocated sectors.

devon: that smells like a false positive from the bloom filter used by the janitor/scanner. we saw something similar with a firmware combo last year (FW 1.2.3 + kernel X). what's nvme fw?

marie: FW: 2.8.1. host reported vendor A.

opsbot: automated-note: 6 nodes in eu-west2-b with nvme3 flagged; autoscaler paused for that AZ until mitigation completes.

vikram: good call on pausing autoscaler. immediate mitigation options: (1) quarantine devices and drain GPU scheduling off those hosts, (2) reduce scrub aggressiveness / disable bloom-check temporarily, (3) schedule targeted firmware downgrade/upgrade, (4) run block-level verify (badblocks) in readonly to confirm. downsides: quarantine reduces available GPU capacity and increases cost for overflow to other AZs.

carla: i'd prefer (2) + (4) to avoid mass node replacement unless badblocks confirm. if it's a bloom false-positive disabling that filter should stop mislabels.

marie: trying (2) now — bumping scrub timeout and turning off bloom-check for this host pool. command: 

```
# on storage-agent config
SCRUB_BLOOM_CHECK=false
SCRUB_MAX_RETRIES=2
systemctl restart storage-scrubber
```

marie: also kicking an on-demand readonly verify: `badblocks -sv /dev/nvme3p1` (will run for ~6m per device). starting on gnode-45, gnode-46 first.

devon: FYI, there's a known metric: if rechecks < 10 and SMART reallocated == 0 and badblocks returns clean, treat as bloom-flap and re-enable bloom after 24h with a softer threshold. we should add that to incident playbook.

marie: badblocks result (gnode-45) — no errors. gnode-46 started and currently 20% through.

vikram: sounds like bloom false-positive. what's causing I/O error lines in dmesg though? could be transient PCI link resets or power management microbursts. check kernel logs for PCIe AER events.

marie: grep shows a few AER messages around the same time: `pcieport AER: Corrected error, id 0001:00:1f.0` — not huge but correlated.

carla: ok, two contributing factors: corrected PCIe errors (transient) + aggressive bloom-check that marks tiny ranges as bad. combined they cause eviction cascade and GPU attach failures. mitigation timeline?

marie: timeline so far: disabled bloom-check (09:10), started badblocks (09:12), quarantined 2 most noisy hosts from scheduling (gnode-45/46) but left them up for verify, autoscaler paused (09:08).

opsbot: note added to runbook: autoscaler paused by opsbot — queueing manual scale up if needed.

devon: propose follow-ups:
- add a probe that cross-validates scrubber bloom hits with badblocks before marking bad (cheap readonly verify for small ranges)
- add a circuit-breaker: if >3 bloom hits within 10m on same device, throttle janitor and alert on PCIe AER rate
- add telemetry to track bloom false-positive rate per FW/kernel combo

carla: agree. also add a temporary routing rule: route new GPU attach requests in eu-west2 to other AZs if attach latency > 2s and devices in pool flagged > 3. helps avoid user-visible failures.

marie: gnode-46 badblocks completed: clean. re-enabled scheduling on both nodes (09:28) but left scrubber in reduced mode. attach success for queued pods confirmed.

vikram: thanks. let's not do mass firmware changes yet. open a follow-up ticket to correlate storage-agent deploy last night with increased bloom sensitivity and check upstream bloom implementation (maybe parameter drift).

devon: ticket created: INFRA-7821 — investigate bloom misclassification, add cross-verify, add telemetry. assign to marie + carla.

marie: quick cost note — we diverted burst jobs to other AZs for ~25 minutes; estimated extra GPU-hours = 6. cost ~ $45. logging for finance.

carla: recorded. also adding temporary flag to deployment pipeline to prevent scrub param changes without a canary window.

opsbot: remediation summary: bloom-check disabled for eu-west2-b scrubbers, readonly badblocks verification run (clean), quarantines lifted, autoscaler unpaused. incident severity: P3, follow-ups assigned.

marie: closing thread — will post RFC for scrub cross-verify and a short postmortem with the numbers. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
